title: Frida Kahlo
passages: Frida Kahlo was born on July 6, 1907, in Coyoacán, a leafy neighborhood of Mexico City. She grew up in a house painted a bright COBALT blue, now known as the Blue House. When she was 18, a bus she was riding in crashed, and she spent months healing in bed. To pass the time, she began to paint. Over her life she made about 200 paintings, and more than 50 of them are PORTRAITS of herself. She often wore flowers in her hair and long, colorful TRADITIONAL dresses from the Tehuantepec region of southern Mexico.

Mexico City has a very long story. It sits where the Aztec capital, TENOCHTITLAN, was founded around 1325 on an island in a lake. The Aztecs grew food on raised garden plots called CHINAMPAS, and families still farm and grow flowers on some of them in Xochimilco today. Now nearly 22 million people live in and around the city, which makes it one of the largest cities in the Americas. Frida died in the Blue House in 1954, and in 1958 it opened as a museum. Today visitors from all over the world walk through her garden, her kitchen and her studio.
